reviewScope: Application source reviewed by build agent; not an independent security audit

High:incorrect-return.reason: Unmodified snarkjs Yul intentionally returns ABI false from the external verifier on invalid field/precompile input. No caller cleanup or state writes are bypassed. Real proof, all public-input/field-bound mutations, malformed points and low-gas tests exercise fail-closed behavior. Exact generated-source comparison is mandatory.

Medium:unused-return.reason: Only the third ECDSA.tryRecover diagnostic argument is discarded. The RecoverError enum and recovered signer are both checked; protocol custom errors intentionally replace the library diagnostic.

Low:timestamp.reason: Timestamps enforce coarse lifecycle deadlines, with no random selection, asset payout or price oracle. Block producer timestamp tolerance is accepted for the demo; operators must use ample windows.

Informational:assembly.reason: Generated Groth16 pairing precompile code and the application modexp inverse wrapper. Inverse checks call success and multiplicative identity; differential and negative tests cover arithmetic.

Informational:cyclomatic-complexity.reason: Commit and close implement explicit protocol guards and three-pair fallback. Covered by lifecycle, fuzz and stateful invariant tests; complexity remains a maintenance risk.

Informational:missing-inheritance.reason: Generated verifier contracts satisfy the fixed-array interfaces structurally. Preserve exact upstream generation; constructors additionally pin verifier runtime code hashes.

Informational:naming-convention.reason: Mathematical coordinates and generated ABI names intentionally follow the circuit/reference notation; no security semantics depend on casing.

Informational:solc-version.reason: Generated sources declare a broad compatibility pragma, but foundry.toml pins the actual compiler to 0.8.30. Generated source is preserved exactly.

Informational:too-many-digits.reason: Compiler-generated runtime bytecode constants are hashed to authenticate actual verifier code, rather than handwritten numeric approximations.
